papers.title: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
papers.abstract: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincaré variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincaré method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection.

papers.title: Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
papers.abstract: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) is conventionally used to probe elementary excitations and correlations in quantum materials. Here, we propose an interferometric RIXS protocol that instead creates entanglement between spatially separated regions of a solid-state material. An incident X-ray photon is coherently split by a beam splitter into two arms illuminating opposite ends of a sample. Recombining the scattered photons at a second beam splitter and detecting an energy-selected photon then projects the material into a coherent superposition of excitations at the two ends. This protocol is the X-ray, solid-state analogue of the Duan-Lukin-Cirac-Zoller (DLCZ) heralding scheme. Using a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism with quantized photon modes, we show that orthogonal and degenerate end excitations yield maximally entangled states. We illustrate this mechanism in three models: (1) two decoupled sites yield a heralded Bell state. (2) An open tight-binding chain exhibits reflection-parity-dependent interference, providing a benchmark for the interferometer's coherence. (3) A spin-1 Haldane (AKLT) chain yields an entangled pair of fractionalized edge spins. We also discuss practical considerations and challenges for realizing the protocol in X-ray experiments.

papers.title: Scaling the Wavelength to Optimize Ultrafast Laser Processing of Bandgap Materials
papers.abstract: The spectral characteristics of ultrashort laser pulses offer unique possibilities to control interactions in space and time as well as the subsequent material responses. In particular, selecting the wavelength predefines the fundamental mechanisms governing laser-matter interaction, and thus, how energy is deposited. This Chapter provides an overview on how the essential physical effects in ultrafast laser-matter interaction scale with the wavelength, and the consequences for bandgap material processing applications. First, we recall the main spectral properties of bandgap materials and discuss the important question of the expected processing resolutions depending on wavelength. Then, recent studies on the impact of the wavelength in ultrafast laser-dielectric interaction are presented. Finally, we present how the latest developments in infrared ultrafast laser sources can be advantageously utilized to internally process narrow-gap materials despite challenges related to increased nonlinearities.

papers.title: Nonclassicality from Incomplete Fock-State Statistics
papers.abstract: Nonclassicality in bosonic systems can be certified directly from occupation probabilities without full state reconstruction. To complete a library of such criteria we introduce a numerical framework that constructs optimal linear nonclassicality witnesses from arbitrary subsets of measured occupation probabilities by solving a semi-infinite linear program. The method contains known analytical criteria as special cases while generally detecting substantially larger nonclassical regions. We provide an open-source implementation of the numerical optimization together with the analytical criteria discussed here, enabling direct application of the framework to measured occupation statistics across bosonic platforms. As a case study, we apply it to the resonant Jaynes--Cummings model with thermal states and reveal nonclassicality at short interaction times and close to thermal balance, where detection of nonclassicality is otherwise challenging.

papers.title: Polarization-encoded photon statistics for counting dipole emitters
papers.abstract: Counting the emitters within a diffraction-limited region is a prerequisite for localizing overlapping molecules. Under pulsed excitation, each molecule emits at most one photon per pulse, so photon-number-resolved detection can count emitters without resolving them. But the required number of pulses grows steeply with the emitter number. Here we show that polarization, conventionally used to measure the orientations of dipole emitters, also carries information on their number. Because mean polarization-resolved signals are unchanged when every emitter is replaced by multiple dimmer copies, this information resides in the photon statistics within each pulse, which polarization reshapes in two ways. Linearly polarized excitation at three angles increases the sub-Poissonian deficit of the photon count by a factor of 1.5 for any emitter orientation, and detection in four polarization channels reveals the emitter number through how the photons of multiphoton pulses are distributed among the channels. Maximum-likelihood simulations for two to five emitters of unknown orientations and brightnesses show that three-angle excitation reduces the required number of pulses by about 2.3-fold, close to the predicted $1.5^2=2.25$, and that adding four-channel detection raises the reduction to as much as 4.8-fold. These gains require only polarization optics added to photon-number-resolved detection.

papers.title: Physics Informed Neural Network for Multi-dimensional Turbulent Self-gravitating Flows
papers.abstract: Molecular clouds exhibit complex, multi-scale dynamics driven by the interplay of turbulence, self-gravity, and gas pressure. Modelling these systems with conventional grid-based methods becomes increasingly expensive as spatial resolution and dimensionality increase. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free alternative by incorporating the governing equations directly into the training objective, but their ability to model realistic turbulent self-gravitating flows remains largely unexplored. We apply PINNs to isothermal molecular clouds initialized with astrophysically motivated turbulent velocity fields, considering subsonic and supersonic evolution in two and three dimensions. We benchmark the predicted density and velocity fields against the finite-volume code Athena++. PINNs accurately recover the global evolution of the flow over multiple free-fall times across turbulent realizations, Mach numbers, and dimensionalities. Their training cost also exhibits weak dependence on spatial resolution, increasing by less than 25% from 128^3 to 1024^3 in our experiments. These results demonstrate that PINNs can model substantially more realistic self-gravitating turbulent flows than previously explored and provide a promising complementary framework for studying these systems.

papers.title: A Compact Single-Beam Optically Pumped Magnetometer Based on Absorption Detection
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a compact single-beam optically pumped magnetometer (OPM) employing a pure 87Rb microfabricated vapor cell with 500 Torr buffer gas. The residual magnetic field is actively minimized to below 400 pT through a combination of mu-metal magnetic shielding and internal compensation coils. We systematically characterize the OPM response as a function of laser detuning and optical intensity, and derive the magnetic-field sensitivity from the signal slope and noise amplitude spectral density. A best sensitivity of 11 fT/Hz^1/2 is achieved near the resonance transition at an optimal optical intensity, using a small cell volume of only 0.027 cm^3. Furthermore, a miniaturized OPM prototype was developed using a folded flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) to integrate the vapor cell, a compact heater, and magnetic-field coils into a cubic sensing head. Two coil configurations patterned directly on the FPCB were investigated. Under optimized operating conditions, the OPM prototype achieved a sensitivity of 66 fT/Hz^1/2. These results demonstrate that high-buffer-pressure single-beam OPMs can achieve excellent sensitivity, establishing a pathway toward compact and scalable arrays.

papers.title: Video-rate quantitative phase and polarimetric imaging (QP2I) for label-free imaging of contracting muscle cells
papers.abstract: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) has become a standard approach for label-free microscopy of transparent specimens, mapping the optical path length. However, the isotropic phase is blind to the molecular order underlying optical anisotropy. Implementations that also add quantitative contrast to birefringence, rely on multi-frame illumination or polarization-state scanning, or on dedicated interferometric hardware, that trade away acquisition speed or the simplicity of a standard microscope. We present Quantitative Phase and Polarimetric Imaging (QP2I), a computational imaging framework that converts a standard differential interference contrast (DIC) microscope with a polarization camera into a single-shot, video-rate, dual-contrast imaging system. We developed a new globally regularized phase reconstruction that eliminates artifacts of prior DIC-to-QPI approaches, providing quantitative phase information and used per-pixel Stokes-based reconstruction to obtain quantitative anisotropic retardance. We validate the approach across simulations, static reference targets, fixed muscle tissue and living dynamically moving cells. Thereby, QP2I enables to study contractile dynamics in live cardiomyocytes all-optically and label-free. It provides both structural and functional readouts at frame rates that are sufficient to temporally resolve fast cardiomyocyte contractions. While conventional fluorescent labels bleach out over time, perturb physiology, and preclude long-term monitoring, QP2I provides similar established structural readouts, such as frame-by-frame sarcomere length, as well as previously inaccessible measurements, like quantitative analysis of retardance changes during muscle contraction, as a direct optical signature of muscle photoelasticity. QP2I thus enables long-term, label-free interrogation of dynamic cellular processes at quantitative contrast.

papers.title: Integrated elliptical III-V nanopillar arrays on silicon for dual photodetection and light emission
papers.abstract: Next-generation on-chip photonic devices require compact, energy-efficient components integrating photodetection and light emission on silicon platforms. Achieving broadband photodetection combined with efficient emission in a single nanoscale device remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate elliptical nanopillar arrays monolithically integrated as III-V-on-Si templates, exhibiting broadband photoresponse across visible to near-infrared wavelengths, dynamic neuron-like graded responses under modulated light, and pronounced electroluminescence at around 865 nm under forward bias. The nanostructured elliptical geometry approach enhances optical absorption and carrier dynamics within an active area significantly smaller than commercial detectors, enabling responsivities up to 0.55 A/W at 830 nm in compact nanoarrays. This work advances the development of miniaturized active nanophotonic devices suitable for integrated sensing, emitting and communication circuits, and neuromorphic processing on silicon substrates.

papers.title: Supercontinuum-driven broadband Fourier-transform photothermal microspectroscopy
papers.abstract: Chemical characterization of microscopic samples often requires resolving multiple, widely separated vibrational absorption bands, including their positions and spectral shapes. Photothermal microspectroscopy provides a route to localized vibrational measurements by detecting absorption-induced thermal responses with a separate optical probe. However, rapid acquisition of broadband photothermal spectra remains challenging when spectral information is collected through sequential wavelength tuning. Here, we develop a supercontinuum (SC)-driven Fourier-transform photothermal (FT-PT) microspectroscopy platform that combines broadband near-infrared excitation with rapid-scan interferometric acquisition for localized vibrational measurements. In this approach, an interferometrically modulated SC pump induces wavelength-dependent photothermal responses in the sample, which are detected through a co-propagating visible probe beam and reconstructed by Fourier transformation. Using a 1.65-2.35 um spectral window, we demonstrate broadband photothermal spectra of aqueous samples with acquisition rates of approximately one spectrum per second. The system simultaneously resolves multiple molecular absorption features in a water-dimethyl sulfoxide mixture and reproduces the near-infrared absorption characteristics of liquid water with high spectral fidelity. Extending beyond homogeneous liquids, a dark-field detection configuration enables broadband photothermal spectroscopy of an individual 6 um polystyrene particle in an aqueous environment. This SC-based FT-PT microspectroscopy approach provides a rapid and broadband platform for localized vibrational characterization of liquid and microscopic samples, enabling chemical analysis with microscale spatial selectivity.

papers.title: Sensitivity-Guided Parameter Estimation of Bubbly Liquid via a Nonlinear Wave Equation and Physics-InformedNeuralNetworks
papers.abstract: Interactions between ultrasound and microbubbles underlie a range of biomedical and industrial applications, yet predicting how the physical parameters of the medium and bubbles govern nonlinear wave propagation remains difficult. This study proposes a parameter estimation framework that combines a Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers (KdVB) equation, describing weakly nonlinear wave propagation in a bubbly liquid, with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The contributions are threefold. First, the PINN reproduces the reference solution of the governing equation in the forward problem, with a near-zero prediction error at the initial time that confirms the initial condition is enforced exactly as intended. Second, prior to inverse estimation, a sensitivity analysis is introduced that quantifies, at both the coefficient and solution levels, how each of eight physical parameters influences the KdVB equation, allowing the expected difficulty of estimating each parameter to be assessed in advance. Third, based on this assessment, single-parameter inverse estimation is performed for seven of the eight parameters using the PINN. Liquid viscosity, bubble initial radius, liquid density, sound speed, and liquid pressure are estimated with errors of 0.8-2.1%, the polytropic exponent converges only partially, and the surface tension coefficient cannot be estimated at all, consistent with the sensitivity analysis. These results establish a general framework for identifying and estimating the physical parameters governing nonlinear wave propagation in bubbly liquids from observed waveform data.

papers.title: Computational imaging through turbid, bubbly and flowing water near the telescope
papers.abstract: Cameras in the surf zone or behind ship wakes look through turbid, bubbly, moving water close to the lens, yet restoration networks are usually scored only on displayed images. We introduce a measured dataset of a telescope viewing displayed images and physical objects through a 25~mm water layer 45~mm in front of its objective, under seven combinations of flow, bubbles and turbidity, with clear-water recordings as a second reference. Because the suspension scatters light far outside the 1.3\textdegree{} field of view, turbidity mainly removes contrast, 4.4- to 4.8-fold on a Siemens star. Restoring the mean of eight frames improves structural similarity (SSIM) by 0.032 over a single frame, and learned fusion of the frames adds little. One raw frame supports five-category recognition (96.8\%) as well as restored images. Adding synthetic training pairs leaves display-image scores unchanged but raises the correlation of a restored Siemens star with its clear-water recording from below 0.5 to above 0.9. These networks also improve ordinary underwater photographs without retraining, where training on measured pairs alone fails. Scoring against the digital source or a clear-water recording reverses the ranking of raw and restored images. These results support a simple pipeline: average the frames, classify raw frames directly, and restore with networks trained on measured and synthetic pairs.

papers.title: Chaos Made Visible: Active particles trace Lorenz-like attractors in physical space
papers.abstract: Chaotic attractors are typically visualized in an abstract phase space. Here we show that an orientable active particle moving through a steady, two-dimensional, multivortex flow can trace a Lorenz-like chaotic attractor in its real space trajectory. Despite the flow being strictly time independent, coupling between particle position and orientation creates a three-dimensional nonlinear dynamical system. For suitable particle shape and swimming speed, the trajectory organizes into a striking two-lobed geometry reminiscent of the classical Lorenz attractor. A structured first return map, positive largest Lyapunov exponent, and a broadband power spectrum establish that the underlying motion is chaotic. Varying the swimming speed reveals a rich sequence of dynamical regimes as self-propulsion breaks streamline confinement and reorganizes the particle motion. Our results demonstrate how an internal orientational degree of freedom can make chaotic dynamics directly visible in physical space, allowing a single active particle to trace a chaotic attractor as it moves through an otherwise steady flow.

papers.title: When does boundary-condition uncertainty outweigh thermal and vegetation effects in street canyon flow? A global sensitivity analysis of input uncertainty
papers.abstract: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is increasingly used to resolve wind, heat, and pollution patterns in cities with high fidelity but high computational cost. Thermal effects and vegetation are often neglected despite being important drivers, yet their influence may be masked by variability from other uncertain inputs. This work determines how precisely model parameters and boundary conditions must be known for these effects to govern output uncertainty in the velocity, temperature, and concentration fields of a two-dimensional street canyon. A global Sobol analysis of 24 parameters is made tractable by a surrogate trained on Reynolds-Averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) simulations, combining principal component analysis (PCA) with multilayer perceptrons (MLPs). Two ventilation regimes assess the variance due to thermal and vegetation parameters as uncertainty in all other inputs is progressively reduced. At typical uncertainty levels, turbulence closure constants and inflow turbulence profiles govern variability in all three fields in both regimes. Under weak ventilation, solar forcing becomes the main source of temperature variability once the remaining uncertainties are halved, and of concentration variance once they are reduced to a quarter (about $\pm11\%$ for the dominant closure constant and $\pm12\%$ for the emission rate). In contrast, vegetation contributes significantly at typical uncertainty levels. Under strong ventilation, however, the canopy never overtakes the closure constants, even when the dominant one is known to $\pm5\%$. Spatially, both effects peak at road level and along canyon walls, which influence outdoor exposure and indoor infiltration, suggesting that high-resolution exposure studies should account for them.

papers.title: Let's Do Turbulence Right: In Space and Time!
papers.abstract: The three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations govern fluid turbulence, a chaotic and non-linear physical phenomenon characterized by complex eddies interacting across vast spatial and temporal scales. A numerically accurate modeling of this multi-scale energy cascade requires fully resolving both the fine spatial structures and the continuous temporal evolution of the flow field. In this paper, we leverage massive, time-resolved direct numerical simulations, which exceed 28 TB per run, to assess how numerical choices govern the resolved (3+1)-dimensional physics of turbulent flows. Building on this analysis, we study how neural networks represent the recorded turbulent motion. Our results highlight that spatial and temporal assessments can disagree for both numerical records and learned representations. We therefore call on the machine learning community to treat (3+1)-dimensional turbulence as a four-dimensional phenomenon.

papers.title: Stochastic Analysis of Laser Phase Noise in Photonics-Assisted Radio Frequency Beamforming
papers.abstract: This paper develops a stochastic model for quantifying the impact of laser phase noise on photonics-assisted radio frequency (RF) beamforming. Unlike conventional deterministic models, the presented theoretical framework captures the statistical randomness associated with the RF array factor of beamforming networks driven by finite-linewidth lasers. Fourier-domain analysis reveals that laser phase noise reshapes the spatial coherence function of such beamforming networks, inducing coherent RF aperture shrinkage, beam-pattern distortion, and directivity degradation. The analysis highlights that beamforming network architectures employing nanosecond-scale optical differential delays can exhibit substantial performance degradation even when driven by commercially available narrow-linewidth (kHz-range) lasers. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that average RF power gain gets downscaled and fluctuations dominate in large-aperture beamforming networks due to phase noise, imposing an upper limit on the maximum achievable RF antenna array-size. The reported results highlight the quantitative performance and scalability limits imposed by laser phase noise in photonics-assisted RF beamforming, offering key design guidelines for implementing large-scale beamforming networks in next-generation wireless communications, sensing, radar, and radio astronomy applications.

papers.title: From Hollow Waveguides to Mie Voids: Low-Index Light Confinement
papers.abstract: The confinement of light within optically thin media challenges the conventional view that optical localization requires high-index dielectric materials and total internal reflection. Over the past decades, a broad range of photonic phenomena has demonstrated that electromagnetic energy can also be guided and localized inside low-index regions or nanoscale void cavities. What first appears to be a curiosity is, in fact, highly relevant: The interaction between light and matter lies at the heart of much in optics and photonics. It enables sensing, nonlinear optical phenomena, and optical manipulation, yet it also inevitably introduces absorption, dissipation, and loss. Pushing localized, enhanced, or guided energy into a lower-index space thus offers entirely new possibilities for light-matter interaction and dispersion control. In this review, we discuss some of these counterintuitive structures, starting with light guidance within optically thin media, such as hollow-core photonic crystal fibers or antiresonant reflecting optical waveguides. We then discuss the optics of bubbles, that is, low-index inclusions in a higher-index surrounding, and ultimately arrive at the so-called Mie void resonators, optical resonators that support localized electromagnetic modes confined within a region of lower refractive index. All these systems demonstrate that there are (resonant) optics beyond simple total internal reflection. Absence can itself become a functional photonic degree of freedom, opening opportunities across sensing, quantum nanophotonics, metasurfaces, and programmable optical matter.

papers.title: Compression of turbulent flow data through an extended space-time correlation: certification against the modal energy budget
papers.abstract: The fidelity of direct numerical simulation now outpaces the storage and data-movement capacity available for the resulting fields. We present an open, distributed, GPU-accelerated low-rank compression framework for large turbulent flow databases. We assess it using two direct numerical simulations of a controlled diffusion compressor cascade under laminar and turbulent inflow conditions. Compression is formulated using a correlation operator over space and time, which is two orders of magnitude larger than that of snapshot POD. Its dominant range is extracted with a randomized range finder based on communication-avoiding hierarchical QR. The compressed databases are evaluated through a hierarchy of increasingly strict diagnostics, from instantaneous reconstruction and second-order statistics to the modal turbulent kinetic energy budget and its nonlinear interscale transfer. The budget terms are far more sensitive to compression than fieldwise or one-point errors. They remain accurate at conservative compression and degrade sharply once the retained energy is relaxed. The near-wall dissipation and the interscale transfer degrade the most and set the admissible compression level. An aggressive reduction preserves every one-point statistic to within a few per cent while corrupting both by an order of magnitude more. The dissipation error is confined to the viscous sublayer and grows with the development of the boundary layer. It is carried by the high-order modes. For both inflows, the linear budget terms scale with the discarded energy to the power $0.8$ and the triadic transfer to a power above one.

papers.title: Electron Wavefronts Capture Nanoscale Movies of Hypersound at Surfaces
papers.abstract: Acoustic waves transport mechanical energy and elastic strain through solids, with material composition and shape governing their propagation. In the gigahertz hypersound regime, acoustic wavelengths reach tens to hundreds of nanometres, comparable to nanoscale device dimensions. Harnessing these waves underpins high-frequency signal processing, sensing, electromagnetic coupling and quantum control. Acoustic metrology probes elastic modes and internal interfaces. Yet directly imaging how nanoscale acoustic waves interact with local structure remains challenging, requiring picometre displacement sensitivity combined with high spatiotemporal resolution. Here we demonstrate full-field imaging of laser-induced hypersound at surfaces using reflected electron wavefronts. We introduce ultrafast low-energy electron microscopy (ULEEM), exploiting the intrinsic surface sensitivity of few-electronvolt electrons. Coherent electron pulses down to femtosecond durations reflect from the topmost atomic layers, imprinting the evolving surface profile onto their wavefronts. Defocus converts phase variations into image contrast. In a thin van der Waals material, we image the thermoelastic generation and propagation of picometre-amplitude acoustic waves. Measured dispersion relations, interpreted through elastodynamic modelling, distinguish substrate-supported and locally detached regions, revealing how interfacial contact shapes propagation. Delayed wave emission reveals scattering at buried mechanical defects. Our results establish electron-wavefront imaging of nanoscale surface dynamics, enabling the exploration of ultrafast energy transport, structural transformations and coupled mechanical, electronic and magnetic phenomena.

papers.title: Revealing and Mitigating Transmittance and Reflectance Errors in Integrating-Sphere Characterization of High-Albedo Scattering Media
papers.abstract: Accurate optical characterization of high-albedo scattering media is fundamentally limited by integrating-sphere measurement errors. Scattering events spatially redistribute photons, leading to lateral beam spread and angular divergence that bias measured reflectance and transmittance. Here, we investigate these deviations, which are quantified and interpreted by using the point spread function (PSF), guided by the radiative transfer equation. Experiments and Monte Carlo modelling show that the widely used external-mount integrating-sphere configuration introduces systematic, configuration-dependent errors that become pronounced when scattering-induced lateral spreading is substantial. Using a normalised PSF to quantify photon redistribution, we map the characteristic lateral spreading length across a broad $(\taus,g)$ parameter space in the high-albedo limit, providing a basis for evaluating errors in specific measurement geometries. We further quantify the influence of measurement geometry and show that, in the pencil-beam limit, maintaining $L/D_{\mathrm{port}}\lesssim 0.01$ reduces the discrepancy arising from the finite collection aperture to approximately \qty{1}{\percent}. In addition, we introduce an internal-mount integrating-sphere protocol that suppresses scattering-related losses and yields transmittance and reflectance measurements in good agreement with theoretical predictions. Overall, our work helps users of integrating-sphere measurements identify scattering-related errors and improve the reliability of transmittance and reflectance characterization across a wide range of application areas.

papers.title: CoPiT: A conditional Position-induced Transformer for aerodynamic field prediction on unstructured meshes
papers.abstract: High-fidelity Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) simulations remain a standard tool for aerodynamic analysis, yet each solve on an unstructured mesh is computationally expensive, making many-query tasks such as design exploration, optimization, and multi-condition evaluation costly. Neural operators provide mesh-flexible surrogates for mapping geometry and operating conditions to flow fields; however, in many existing architectures, global parameters such as the freestream state and design variables are concatenated with pointwise inputs, leaving their influence on intermediate features implicit. This paper proposes CoPiT, a \textbf{Co}nditional \textbf{P}osition-induced \textbf{T}ransformer that builds on the Position-induced Transformer (PiT) as its geometric backbone and injects a global condition vector through multi-stage feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), thereby making parametric modulation explicit while preserving geometry-based attention weights. The model is evaluated on two-dimensional AirfRANS airfoil fields, including scarce-data and extrapolation regimes, and on three-dimensional BlendedNet++ blended-wing-body surfaces. On the AirfRANS full-data test set, CoPiT reduces surface and volume losses by approximately 54\% and 24\% relative to Transolver, respectively, and achieves the lowest overall normalized test MSE among the compared baselines on BlendedNet++. Matched ablations show that FiLM conditioning generally improves upon input concatenation, while the preferred placement is task-dependent. CoPiT thus provides a practical operator-learning surrogate for parametric aerodynamics on unstructured meshes.

papers.title: High Resolution Hyperspectral Quantum Infrared Imaging with Undetected Photons
papers.abstract: Quantum sensing in the infrared regime often demands the use of expensive and cryogenically operated detectors. Nonlinear interferometry has paved the way for information transfer from the infrared to the near--infrared or visible regime in various quantum technologies. A particularly interesting application of these interferometers involves spectrally--resolved quantum imaging using undetected photons, enabled by the use of temperature--tunable parametric amplifiers. In this work, we demonstrate spectrally resolved transmission imaging with undetected photons around 1550 nm using a spontaneous parametric down conversion based folded nonlinear interferometric scheme, registering the attenuation of a zebrafish larva as a biological feasibility test. We characterize and calibrate the interferometer, having achieved spectrally resolved interference fringes with a maximum baseline visibility of $\sim 74\%$ in the near--infrared regime. Phase--stepped readout of a grating spectrometer gives a resolving power of $\sim1460$ (from the spectrometer's point spread function) at 1550 nm, and $\sim 730$ from the coherence length, the finest reported for imaging with undetected photons, over an instantaneous spectral window of $\approx 51$ cm$^{-1}$.

papers.title: Bogoliubov Dynamics and Zitterbewegung in Optical Dirac Systems
papers.abstract: We develop a bosonic Bogoliubov description of Zitterbewegung in time-dependent optical-Dirac systems. Within the optical-Dirac framework, the anomalous pair-creation and pair-annihilation terms of a bosonic Bogoliubov Hamiltonian correspond to couplings between the positive- and negative-frequency sectors, whose coherence underlies the Zitterbewegung response. When the constitutive parameters vary in time, the resulting moving-frame connection generates dynamical interbranch coupling and positive--negative-frequency coherence. Under periodic modulation, this coupling becomes resonant near $Ω\simeq2ω_0$, leading to parametric amplification of the coherence and consequently to an enhanced Zitterbewegung motion.

papers.title: Solving and Learning Navier-Stokes Dynamics with the Neural Basis Method
papers.abstract: Physics-informed machine learning has become a major direction in predictive modeling of fluid dynamics, combining governing physics with learned representations. Yet prevailing formulations neither guarantee that small PDE-residual losses imply small solution errors nor scale effectively with increasing problem size. Here we present the neural basis method (NBM) as a new approach for Navier--Stokes dynamics. NBM is built on a ``representation-then-projection'' principle: fixed neural bases define the representation space, while projection of the governing equations determines the expansion coefficients. The same bases define common coordinates for the parametric solution manifold, recasting operator learning as a parameter-to-coefficient mapping and enabling scalability by removing explicit spatial dependence. For incompressible flow, NBM yields a velocity-only formulation whose residual provides an a posteriori velocity-error estimate, establishing a certified, data-free training objective for coefficient learning. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, generalization, and scalability of NBM, with substantial improvements over baselines.

papers.title: Heat vortices and the vorticity triplet in kinetic phonon transport: a fluid-dynamical perspective
papers.abstract: From a novel fluid-dynamical perspective, the present study investigates the heat-current vortices and heat vorticity in heat conduction process of solid materials. The heat vorticity $\bmω$, defined as the curl of the heat-flux field, is decomposed into the orbital-rotation $\bm{R}$ and spin $\bm{S}$, which collectively constitute the heat-vorticity triplet $(\bm{R},\bm{S},\bmω)$, extending beyond the existing single-vorticity research paradigm. As an illustrative example, kinetic phonon transport in a 2D porous solid structure is examined based on the numerical solutions of the Peierls-Boltzmann equation under the Callway dual-relaxation-time approximation. The physical characteristics of heat vortices and the vorticity triplet patterns are analyzed across different kinetic regimes in the phase diagram of the normal (N) and resistive (R) scattering processes.... In the hydrodynamic limit, the boundary generation mechanism of heat vorticity is further elucidated based on the Guyer-Krumhansl (G-K) equation generated from the truncated Chapman-Enskog (C-E) expansion. The boundary heat vorticity flux (BHVF) is proposed as a new concept for describing the local rate at which heat vorticity is generated at the boundary of a solid material. The general expression for the BHVF is rigorously derived for phonon hydrodynamics, and for the 2D steady hydrodynamic phonon transport case, we find that the BHVF is solely attributed to the tangential component of the net heat flux deviating from the classical Fourier heat flux. Furthermore, we show that the total vorticity contained in a control volume arises from the spatiotemporal accumulation of the BHVF, weighted by the memory kernel arising from the R scattering. The proposed theory and findings herein could be valuable for understanding the diverse vortical-flow phenomena in condensed matter systems.

papers.title: IMRFit: Interactive Simulation and Constitutive-Model Fitting for Inertial Microcavitation Rheometry
papers.abstract: Inertial microcavitation rheometry (IMR) characterizes the high-rate mechanical response of soft materials from the rapid expansion and collapse of a microscopic bubble. In a typical IMR experiment, high-speed imaging provides the bubble radius as a function of time, R(t), and material parameters are identified by comparing the measured response with simulations that couple bubble dynamics to a constitutive description of the surrounding medium. This inverse analysis requires repeated forward simulations and careful control of experimental inputs, material parameters, and fitting settings. IMRFit is an open-source Python desktop application that brings these steps into an interactive environment for forward simulation, parameter identification, and constitutive-model comparison. Users can import experimental radius-time data, select a bubble-dynamics formulation and constitutive model, inspect simulated responses, fit material parameters, and organize batch fitting and parameter-sweep jobs. IMRFit includes Neo-Hookean Kelvin-Voigt and generalized Maxwell-Ogden-based models, among other constitutive options, and supports additional models through JSON descriptors and Python solver entry points. It also integrates fitting-window selection, visualization, and data export into a single workflow.

papers.title: Robustness of Quantum Correlations and Controlled Teleportation Fidelity under Noisy Channels
papers.abstract: In distributed quantum computing, quantum networks provide a potential infrastructure for long-range quantum information processing. Controlled quantum teleportation (CQT) is a key practically relevant protocol that can connect two parties on a network and enables a third party, the controller to allow or abort the secure teleportation of an arbitrary single-qubit state between the two parties. We investigate the robustness of a three-qubit GHZ resource under bit-flip, phase-flip, depolarizing, and amplitude-damping noise. Using the Kraus-operator formalism, we characterize the noisy resource through multipartite quantum discord, genuine multipartite concurrence (GMC), localizable entanglement (LE), and CQT fidelity. We also outline a proof-of-concept photonic implementation for preparing the three-qubit GHZ resource and realizing the CQT protocol, which could enable experimental investigation of the effects of noise. Our results show that bit-flip and amplitude-damping noise generally preserve useful mutipartite quantum correlations over broader noise parameter ranges. Interestingly, multipartite discord exhibits freezing under bit-flip noise over a finite parameter regime. Moreover, discord can persist beyond the sudden death of genuine multipartite entanglement, revealing the distinct robustness of nonclassical correlations. We further demonstrate that CQT fidelity which characterizes the performance of CQT can exceed the classical threshold even after GMC vanishes, while LE more closely reflects the operational usefulness of the noisy resource. These findings highlight the complementary roles of quantum correlations and entanglement in assessing the resilience of GHZ-based protocols.

papers.title: Cross-coupled photon avalanche drives room-temperature intrinsic optical bistability
papers.abstract: Optically bistable materials promise technological advances in optical information processing, memristive devices, and multiparametric sensing. However, optical bistability is predominantly observed under cryogenic conditions or is governed by subtle thermo-optical nonlinearities. Here, we report on Ho3+-activated nanocrystals that exhibit cavity-free intrinsic optical bistability (IOB) at ambient conditions. Non-thermal IOB stems from a cross-coupled photon avalanche (XPA) mechanism enabled by a low-phonon-energy double-perovskite host, which reduces nonradiative losses and facilitates excited-state population via XPA, even when the pump intensity is below threshold. Time-resolved luminescence measurements support the proposed XPA, as evidenced by a double-rise profile consistent with two reservoir states interlocked in energy looping. IOB with high-contrast photoswitching (up to 46 dB) is observed at room temperature across multiple visible emission lines, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing and compatibility with common detectors. IOB is preserved across nano- to microscale crystals and different double-perovskite compositions, broadly enabling information photonics and advanced sensing.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) approximations of capillary menisci in polygonal channels
papers.abstract: In a zero-gravity cylindrical container, a meniscus can span a square or equilateral-triangular cross-section only at contact angles at or above the respective Concus-Finn critical angles of 45 degrees and 60 degrees. We study strong-form physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) across these thresholds under fixed collocation and optimization budgets. Classical capillary flux balance yields a lower bound on the combined interior and wall residual loss for arbitrary positive sampling densities. In the tested nonexistence regime, several degrees below the critical angles, independently evaluated network losses are 1.6-1.9 times this bound. A polynomial least-squares comparison supports the same geometric interpretation. The PINNs still return smooth graphs with finite axial extent, even though the prescribed equilibrium problem has no spanning graph solution. Their small interior residuals coexist with wall-flux deficits near corners, where adjoining contact-angle conditions demand more flux than a finite-slope graph can supply. Residuals vary on both sides of the critical angle, while the bound tends uniformly to zero at threshold for fixed wall weight. These results give a geometric scale for interpreting the computed loss and locate the incompatibility that a small interior residual can conceal.

papers.title: Anchored HLLD: A Riemann solver for a hypoelastic diffuse-interface model of compressible fluid-solid interaction
papers.abstract: We present an HLLD Riemann solver for a multicomponent hypoelastic diffuse-interface model of compressible fluid-solid interaction, with no separately computed interface and a deviatoric stress advanced by an objective hypoelastic rate law outside conservation-law form. The difficulty specific to this model is that the stress evolution is nonconservative and, unlike the familiar volume-fraction terms of Kapila-type models, cannot be left outside the Riemann solve once the shear waves are resolved. The shear coefficient $ρ(G+τ_{xx})$ sets the impedance of the resolved shear waves and so belongs to their eigenstructure. Anchored HLLD carries it inside the solve by evaluating the HLLD fan twice at each face, anchored in turn to each adjacent cell-centered state, with every cell advancing from the flux anchored to its own state. HLL, HLLC, and anchored HLLD form a three-tier hierarchy of increasing wave resolution in one framework. We prove local structural properties: consistency at the reconstruction order, exact species-mass conservation, and tangential-momentum and energy drift vanishing under refinement at the reconstruction's face-jump order on smooth fields, with one-dimensional tests illustrating these structural properties and demonstrating first-order drift convergence on discontinuous fields. Across one-dimensional tests and two-dimensional production simulations in the open-source solver MFC, anchored HLLD resolves both the material contact and the shear waves, HLLC the contact alone, and HLL neither sharply. Where refinement studies are shown, anchored HLLD converges toward exact or semi-analytic solutions. A three-dimensional shock-ellipsoid interaction demonstrates the solver with all six stress components active.

papers.title: Reversal of a flat plate into its wake: a minimal model for wake capture
papers.abstract: In reciprocating flapping-like motions, wing-wake interaction plays a crucial role in fluid force generation. While this effect's existence has been acknowledged, particularly in explaining discrepancies between measured forces and quasi-steady approximations, fundamental research on the mechanism underlying this interaction and its scaling remains limited. To address this, we investigate the excess drag force, relative to quasi-steady estimates, acting on a flat plate during the reversal phase of a forward and back translational motion. The flow produced by this motion, studied at insect-flight-relevant Reynolds numbers, serves as a simplified analogue to biological flapping. We demonstrate that interaction with pre-existing wake flow indeed generates excess drag. The main parameter governing this interaction is the distance travelled before reversal, which influences both magnitude and temporal dynamics of the peak drag. We link our observations to optimal vortex formation, as the time trace of the additional drag during reversal is qualitatively altered by the detachment of the starting vortex ring: vortex detachment and re-formation lead to two distinct wake-force peaks. Furthermore, as the pre-reversal distance traversed increases, the wake interaction force post-reversal decays more slowly. Flow observations reveal a similar spatial decay of the streamwise velocity in the wake at the moment of reversal, suggesting a direct link. Representing the starting vortex as a point vortex indicates that the wake's spatial scaling, and commensurately the temporal scaling of the wing-wake interaction effect, is primarily governed by the vortex ring position, shape, and circulation. This simplification reveals a dependence on the pre-reversal translation distance that can be described by a combined fourth-root and linear scaling.

papers.title: Parasitic Interference in Heterodyne Interferometers: Modeling, Characterization, and Mitigation
papers.abstract: Parasitic interference is a common limitation in laser interferometers, arising from unwanted beams that corrupt the phase measurement and degrade displacement sensitivity. In this work, we present a unified framework for the characterization and mitigation of parasitic interference in heterodyne interferometers. Parasitic beams are classified into two types based on the orientation of their corresponding phase vectors, and their noise contribution is modeled as a function of polarization, relative amplitude, and phase of the parasitic beam. Central to this framework is the concept of coupling coefficients, which quantify the interferometer's susceptibility to parasitic interference and can be readily computed using Jones calculus for any optical configuration. The two types of parasitic interference motivate distinct mitigation strategies: differential interferometry and balanced detection, complemented by polarization control and high-quality beam splitters. The models and mitigation strategies are validated experimentally in both a simplified Mach-Zehnder interferometer and a differential interferometer used for optomechanical inertial sensing, demonstrating reductions in parasitic phase noise by up to four orders of magnitude and achieving sub-picometer displacement sensitivity at frequencies as low as 9 mHz under ambient atmospheric pressure.

papers.title: DO-CGI: deep-optimized illumination patterns for computational ghost imaging at low sampling ratios
papers.abstract: Computational ghost imaging (CGI) reconstructs objects from known illumination patterns and bucket-detector measurements, but quality deteriorates at low sampling ratios (SRs). We present a deep-learning framework that optimizes grayscale diffuser patterns before reconstruction. In simulations using CIFAR-10 and MNIST images with Split Bregman reconstruction, the learned patterns outperform random patterns in peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity, including at SRs below 5\%. Patterns trained on CIFAR-10 also transfer to MNIST and remain effective under moderate perturbations of the sensing matrix. These results support learned pattern design as a route to fewer CGI measurements.

papers.title: Sideband-Resolved 4H-SiC Optomechanical Resonators with Interference-Engineered Anchor-Loss Suppression
papers.abstract: Sideband-resolved cavity optomechanical resonators provide a powerful platform for coherent photon--phonon interactions, enabling applications ranging from quantum state transduction and optomechanically induced transparency to precision sensing and microwave photonics. Achieving this regime in integrated microresonators, however, requires simultaneously realizing a narrow optical cavity linewidth, a high-frequency mechanical mode, and low mechanical dissipation. Here, we report the first sideband-resolved optomechanical resonators based on the 4H silicon carbide (4H-SiC) platform. By combining compact microdisk geometries with interference-engineered anchor-loss suppression, we simultaneously achieve intrinsic optical quality factors exceeding $1\times10^6$, room-temperature mechanical quality factors up to $1.51\times10^4$, and a sideband-resolution factor greater than seven. Systematic numerical and experimental studies reveal that a local minimum in anchor loss enables high mechanical quality factors without requiring aggressive undercutting, substantially improving fabrication yield and device robustness. We further demonstrate the first observation of optomechanically induced transparency in integrated 4H-SiC resonators, confirming coherent cavity optomechanical interactions in this material platform. These results establish 4H-SiC as a promising platform for integrated cavity optomechanics and provide a practical route toward scalable photon--phonon devices for classical and quantum photonic technologies.

papers.title: Universal mapping of drop impact spreading from wetting to Leidenfrost regimes
papers.abstract: We establish a universal mapping between the maximum spreading of a drop under wetting and Leidenfrost impact conditions from an energy-dissipation perspective, with the latter featuring a stable vapor film between the drop and the substrate. Experiments and direct numerical simulations demonstrate that the mapping remains valid over two to three orders of magnitude in the Ohnesorge and Weber numbers. This framework provides a simple route for converting established predictions for wetting impacts into their Leidenfrost counterparts, with implications for predicting and controlling droplet impact.

papers.title: A Two-Regime Statistical Framework for Wind-Power Distributions: From Wind-Speed Fluctuations to Turbine Control
papers.abstract: Wind-power variability is a major challenge for the reliable integration of utility-scale wind energy into modern power systems. Although wind-speed statistics are often described by simple parametric distributions, translating these statistics into turbine-level power fluctuations is nontrivial because the relationship between wind speed and power is highly nonlinear and changes across different turbine operating regimes. Here, we develop a two-regime statistical framework for wind-power distributions. In the aerodynamic operating regime, between the cut-in and rated speeds, the turbine power follows an approximate cubic dependence on wind speed. Starting from a physically motivated Rician model for the wind-speed magnitude, we derive an analytical expression for the corresponding wind-power distribution using a nonlinear change of variables. In the control-dominated near-rated regime, where active blade-pitch and generator control regulate the turbine output, the aerodynamic transformation is no longer applicable. Instead, we characterize the power deficit relative to the rated power and show empirically that its continuous tail is well described by a bounded stretched-exponential distribution for both individual turbines and wind-farm ensembles. These results provide a physically interpretable statistical description of wind-power fluctuations across the full operational range of utility-scale wind turbines.

papers.title: Calibration of scintillator-based X-ray detectors for broadband laser-driven X-ray radiation
papers.abstract: Laser-driven X-ray sources produce broadband radiation with substantial shot-to-shot fluctuations, requiring calibrated detector-response models for quantitative measurements of photon fluence and spectral distribution. Scintillator-based flat-panel detectors, originally developed primarily for medical and industrial X-ray imaging, are increasingly being adopted for diagnostics of laser-plasma-based X-ray sources because they provide large-area, spatially resolved detection. We report the calibration of two complementary X-ray detector systems: a CsI:Tl-based flat-panel detector and a plastic-scintillator filter-stack spectrometer intended for spectral reconstruction. Both detectors were characterized using well-defined ISO 4037 N-series reference radiation qualities, providing controlled polychromatic X-ray fields for establishing their signal response and signal-to-fluence conversion.

papers.title: Topological Classification of Non-Normalizable Vector Fields
papers.abstract: Topological classification of physical vector fields conventionally relies on field normalization and homotopy-based invariants. However, when field amplitudes vanish, normalization becomes ill-defined, preventing a direct topological characterization. Here, we introduce a general framework for the topological classification of non-normalizable $n$-dimensional vector fields with compactifiable base spaces by transforming them into $(n+1)$-dimensional normalized vector fields. This construction extends homotopy-based classification to fields containing amplitude zeros. We explicitly demonstrate the approach for one-, two-, and three-dimensional non-normalized vector fields and derive the corresponding topological invariants. The resulting topological charges are robust under continuous deformations and can change only when the embedding structure becomes singular. Our framework provides a unified route to the topological characterization of non-normalizable fields and opens the door to the study of topological phenomena in a broad range of systems, including magnetic textures, ferroelectrics, electromagnetic fields, and wave systems.

papers.title: Rician Distribution as a Physically Interpretable Model for Wind-Speed Statistics
papers.abstract: The statistics of atmospheric wind variations are commonly modeled using Gaussian or Weibull forms, which often trade physical interpretability against statistical accuracy, especially in the distribution tails. Here we derive a Rician distribution for wind speed from a simple physical model based on two orthogonal Gaussian velocity components with a non-zero mean in the preferred direction. Using wind-speed records from four geographically distinct wind farms, we show that the Rician model consistently outperforms the Gaussian model and remains competitive with the Weibull model. The same behavior persists when the data are partitioned into monthly windows, where the Rician parameters also provide a transparent description of seasonal and geographic variability, compared to Weibull parameters. In addition, the model naturally connects Gaussian-like and Weibull-like regimes through the Rician parameter ratio $μ/σ$, making the Rician distribution a compact and physically interpretable two-parameter model for wind-speed statistics.

papers.title: Time-Reversal Invariant Topological Photonic Alloy
papers.abstract: Conventional approaches generate quantum spin Hall (QSH) and quantum valley Hall (QVH) effects by breaking spatial inversion symmetry across the entire photonic crystal. Consequently, modulating the bulk transmission gaps within these periodic frameworks typically requires global modification of structural parameters throughout the lattice, severely limiting device reconfigurability and post-fabrication adaptability. In this work, we demonstrate that global inversion symmetry breaking is not a prerequisite for inducing topological phases. Instead, local and minimal symmetry breaking is sufficient. Using a photonic alloy platform based on random substitutional disorder in a parallel-plate waveguide, we show that a disorder-driven local breaking of z-direction mirror symmetry and a local breaking of in-plane symmetry are capable of opening topological gaps to trigger QSH and QVH phase transitions, respectively, thereby supporting robust helical edge states and valley kink states. Rigorous topological characterization via the reflection-phase winding method reveals a striking size-dependent scaling behavior in both configurations, where the threshold doping concentration required to trigger the topological phase transition asymptotically vanishes in the thermodynamic limit. By enabling flexible, on-demand bulk gap engineering simply through random doping tuning rather than global structural reconfigurations, this photonic alloy platform not only deepens understanding of disorder induced topological physics but also offers a scalable, highly efficient design strategy for integrated topological optical communications.

papers.title: Small-scale polarization variations in near-inertial deep Mediterranean horizontal waterflow
papers.abstract: Deep-sea observations are reported of horizontal waterflow differences with typical amplitudes of 0.02 m s-1 over 50-m small scales so that relative vorticity reaches values of the inertial frequency f. The timeseries observations are made using a complex mooring system deployed in the 2500-m deep Mediterranean Sea, where vertical density stratification is extremely weak, with buoyancy frequency O(f), and the slow waterflow with total speeds <0.07 m s-1 is dominated by inertial internal waves and sub-mesoscale eddies. Horizontal waterflow differences increase when polarization, i.e. direction of traversal of elliptic oscillatory motion, switches sign. Common anticyclonic polarization of inertial motions is predominantly found under near-homogeneous conditions. It alternates with uncommon cyclonic polarization under stratified-water conditions, varyingly over 50-m distances. The alternation is in line with predictions from non-traditional inertio-gravity wave theory, but only when relatively strong turbulent convection causes local reduced stratification, as observed.

papers.title: Laser induced optical reconfiguration in Ge_Sb_Te Films with composition dependent response
papers.abstract: Phase change Ge_Sb_Te (GST) materials exhibit pronounced optical contrast and tunability driven by structural transformations, enabling a diverse range of photonic and optoelectronic applications. GST materials undergo reversible amorphous crystalline phase transitions during which the refractive index and extinction coefficient increase significantly in the crystalline phase across a broad spectral range. However, a systematic correlation between local composition, crystalline microstructure, and broadband optical response within as deposited crystalline GST films has not been established, particularly for films spanning various compositions within a single growth process and in the absence of amorphous-crystalline transitions. Here, we report a systematic study of composition resolved optostructural property relationships in as-deposited crystalline GST films spanning Ge3Sb2Te6, Ge2Sb2Te5, and GeSb2Te4 within a single CVD process, avoiding intermediate phase transitions. This enables direct correlations between composition, microstructure, morphology, and broadband optical response across 400-1700 nm. Specifically, the compositional gradient results in a shift of the absorption minimum from 815.9 nm to 889.8 nm, accompanied by a 5.9 fold change in the intensity, reflecting the strong dependence of optical behavior on composition and microstructure. We further show that femtosecond laser irradiation enables spatially selective tuning of the optical response. These findings establish crystalline GST films as a platform for broadband-tunable, spatially programmable photonic elements, controllable through both compositional design and localized laser processing.

papers.title: Antichiral hinge states in a higher-order photonic nodal ring semimetal
papers.abstract: Antichiral states propagate in the same direction on opposite boundaries, defying the conventional constraint that boundary modes must cancel net chirality. Previously found antichiral states have been limited to first-order topological semimetals. However, antichiral hinge states, the antichiral counterpart of recently discovered higher-order chiral hinge states, remain elusive. Here, we report the observation of antichiral hinge states in a higher-order nodal-ring semimetal made of a three-dimensional gyromagnetic photonic crystal. Near-field scanning measurements reveal a pair of hinge states at two parallel one-dimensional boundaries propagating unidirectionally along the same direction, with robust transport against metallic scatterers. Their spatial positions can be reconfigured by adding or removing photonic layers. The additionally observed antichiral and drumhead surface states manifest a hierarchy of first- and second-order topological boundary states within a single photonic system. Our work extends antichiral states to higher-order topological semimetals and has potential applications in robust and reconfigurable photonic routing.

papers.title: Theory of Cubic-Phase Dynamics in the Linear Potential
papers.abstract: A quantum wave packet in a linear potential, i.e., under a constant force such as gravity, accumulates a cubic-in-time phase that is universal across Schrodinger-type platforms and naturally realized by Airy eigenstates. Because the classical action is quadratic in the force, this phase comprises exactly three contributions: intrinsic, force-induced, and a cross term. The force-induced contribution alone is shape-independent, whereas the Airy eigenstate renders the shape-dependent contributions non-dispersing. An eigenstate-based nondimensionalization identifies the eigenforce, namely the intrinsic force underlying the packet's acceleration in the absence of an applied force, as a natural parameter. As a function of both forces, the cubic coefficient takes an analytically closed and physically interpretable form that factors along two zero lines: the static Airy eigenstate and a nontrivial zero at which the phase cancels without stationarity. This exposes the eigenforce as an effective antagonist to the applied force, not only in the caustic's self-acceleration but also within the phase, while leaving the centroid unaffected in accordance with Ehrenfest's theorem. Spatially uniform within each packet, the phase cannot be measured directly and is accessible only through the relative phase of two colliding packets, each evolving in its own potential. The general relative cubic coefficient, forbidden by symmetry for identical packets and activated by preparation asymmetry, therefore provides a designable signal. Extracted through heterodyne demodulation of the simulated interference between two Airy packets, its central value agrees with the prediction to sub-percent accuracy within the fitting uncertainty. The analysis spans ultracold-atom condensates, paraxial optics, and surface-gravity water waves.

papers.title: Testing the Anton-Schmidt dark energy model with the DESI DR2 measurements
papers.abstract: We present a comparative cosmological analysis of the Anton-Schmidt, $Λ$CDM, and CPL models using baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 2, combined with the Planck PR4 (NPIPE) CamSpec Cosmic Microwave Background likelihoods and three Type Ia supernova catalogues: Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, and Union3. We use Markov Chain Monte Carlo analyses to constrain the parameters of the Anton-Schmidt model against each dataset combination. We find that the Anton-Schmidt model provides a good fit to current cosmological observations. The Anton-Schmidt model provides a good fit to the current cosmological observations but does not provide a significant alleviation of either the $H_0$ or the $S_8$ tensions. The Anton-Schmidt parameter is tightly constrained to $B \simeq -0.38$, indicating that the logarithmic correction becomes relevant only at late times. The Anton-Schmidt and CPL models predict quintessence-like present-day dark-energy equations of state and shows Quintom-B evolution, with their dark-energy equation-of-state parameters crossing the phantom divide at approximately $z \approx 0.5$. The characteristic density scale is constrained to be $ρ_\ast/ρ_{c,0}\sim4\text{--}5$, substantially smaller than the large density scales typically assumed in logotropic-inspired scenarios, indicating that the Anton-Schmidt correction mainly affects the late-time expansion history. Finally, Bayesian evidence shows moderate-to-strong preference for the Anton-Schmidt model over the $Λ$CDM model and strong-to-decisive preference over the CPL parametrization. Although the Anton-Schmidt model does not alleviate the current cosmological tensions, it emerges as a statistically favored dynamical dark-energy scenario whose cosmological implications deserve further tested with forthcoming Stage-IV large-scale structure observations.

papers.title: The Information Rate of Fiber-Wireless Communication Systems Based on Photonic Generation of RF Signals
papers.abstract: High-capacity fiber-wireless communication systems operating at high frequencies increasingly rely on photonic generation of radio-frequency (RF) signals. In these systems, optical signals are transmitted over optical fibers and detected by photodetectors, where RF signals are generated at frequencies equal to the difference between the optical carrier frequencies. A major performance-limiting impairment is the phase noise of the generated RF signals, which originates from the phase noise of the optical sources. In this paper, we develop comprehensive probabilistic models for the two principal configurations of fiber-wireless communication systems employing photonic RF generation. Based on these models, we propose an efficient numerical framework for calculating the information rate (IR). Numerical simulations are performed to validate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm and the results provide design guidelines for high-performance fiber-wireless systems.

papers.title: Foundations of a solved-volatility stochastic turbulence closure: Itô--Hencky kinematics, source-consistent momentum and finite-correlation realisation
papers.abstract: Most stochastic closures prescribe a covariance tensor, a noise basis or an eddy-viscosity field. This paper develops a different framework in which the displacement-volatility field is solved together with the resolved velocity. The starting point is a one-channel Itô configuration map. A local matrix-logarithm expansion gives distinct material and spatial Hencky increments, their quadratic-variation drifts and the exact pathwise volume constraint. Under constant density, one Brownian channel, pathwise isochoricity and no independent martingale in the resolved Eulerian drift, the material pull-back momentum equation is shown to be the on-shell form of the full stochastic Reynolds transport balance when the momentum-source covariation is retained. The resulting velocity--volatility--pressure system has an index-one differential--algebraic structure. Virtual power fixes the mechanical type of the stress impulse and separates work from quadratic covariation. A finite-correlation precursor then gives a Green--Kubo realisation of the solved displacement covariance. State dependence adds a Lyapunov noise-induced drift, while dynamic boundaries add reaction work and active/passive covariance compatibility conditions. The analysis also gives four limits: a non-zero Brownian transport limit cannot retain finite ordinary unresolved kinetic energy; total energy alone does not fix entropy production; wall tangency limits covariance rank rather than the number of stochastic modes; and a homogeneous decoupled Helmholtz--Stokes equation has only the trivial periodic solution. The result is a theory-complete, testable closure architecture. Developed turbulent statistics, logarithmic wall scaling and computational-fluid-dynamics validation are deliberately left to the expanded fluid-mechanics study.

papers.title: Geometry resolved atomic oxygen risk assessment for very low earth orbit spacecraft
papers.abstract: Atomic oxygen (AO) is a major durability concern for spacecraft in very low Earth orbit (VLEO), yet orbit-averaged fluence does not resolve exposure on individual surfaces and internal components. This study develops a geometry-resolved AO assessment by coupling NRLMSISE-00, HWM07, and SYSTEMA ATOMOX. One-year simulations were performed for a 350 km circular Sun-synchronous orbit at LTAN 06:00 and 12:00 using a baseline spacecraft, a wedge-modified body, and two synthetic aperture radar antenna sub-arrays. The LTAN 12:00 orbit produced 8-10% higher orbit-averaged AO flux than LTAN 06:00. For the baseline geometry, the ram-facing surface accumulated 6.9-7.5 x 10^21 atoms/cm^2, whereas side and zenith/nadir surfaces received only 3-5% of the ram fluence. Material-specific erosion yields changed the component-level risk ranking: the CFRP zenith panel was predicted to erode by 15.1-16.2 um/year despite receiving much lower fluence than the ram-facing multilayer insulation. The wedge generated approximately one order of magnitude spatial variation through local shielding. Housing openings also allowed AO to reach internal printed circuit boards, with maximum annual fluences of 9.5 x 10^16 and 4.0 x 10^19 atoms/cm^2 in the H- and V-polarized antenna models, respectively. HWM07 winds produced 10-20% side-panel asymmetry, which decreased below 1% when winds were disabled. Comparison with MISSE-8 reproduced the measured zenith-to-ram ratio of approximately 4% but underpredicted wake exposure, identifying a limitation of ballistic ray tracing. These results demonstrate that VLEO AO durability requires coupled consideration of orbit, atmospheric winds, geometry, and material response.

papers.title: Synthesis of hybrid gold-protein nanobioconjugates with strongly enhanced circular dichroism
papers.abstract: Controlling chiral light-matter interactions with nanophotonics is a powerful strategy for amplifying molecular circular dichroism (CD) beyond its natural limits. Here, we present a plasmonic platform that uses superchiral near fields to amplify the optical activity of biological chromophores. Gold nanoparticles (3.6 nm in diameter) are electrostatically coupled with photosynthetic proteins which results in stable hybrid nanobioconjugates in aqueous solution. The Q-band absorption spectrum of the proteins overlaps with the localized surface plasmon resonance of the gold particles. In the visible region, a combination of numerical simulations and normalized CD measurements reveal an enhancement factor of 3 compared to free proteins. This observation reveals three effects. First, there is a local increase in electromagnetic chirality density in the protein environment. Second, there is an increase in the absorption of the proteins. Third, there is plasmon-induced circular dichroism. Our results quantitatively demonstrate that near-field super-chirality directly modulates biomolecular optical activity. These findings open new avenues for chiroptical nanodevices, biosensing platforms, and light-driven asymmetric photochemistry.

papers.title: A universal diffuse interface modeling framework for surfactants
papers.abstract: We propose a universal diffuse-interface modeling framework for surfactant transport in two-phase flows, applicable to all solubility scenarios and to any conservative phase field method. The foundation of our framework is a general three-scalar non-equilibrium model governing the surfactant concentrations in each bulk phase and at the interface, which builds on our prior consistent scalar transport framework and is locally and globally conservative, leakage-free, Galilean-invariant, and reduction-consistent. Assuming thermochemical equilibrium, we derive two one-scalar models: one for a surfactant in full equilibrium between both bulk phases and the interface, and one for a surfactant confined to a single bulk phase and the interface. All models are coupled to the Navier-Stokes equations through a surface tension force that incorporates the Marangoni stress arising from non-uniform interfacial surfactant distributions. While diffuse-interface surfactant models have been developed for the Cahn-Hilliard equation and, more recently, for the conservative Allen-Cahn (CAC) equation, existing models for CAC address only the insoluble and single-phase-soluble cases, leaving the general scenario of partial solubility in both bulk phases unaddressed; furthermore, these models lack Galilean invariance and reduction consistency, and are not applicable beyond the CAC setting. The framework is validated against analytical solutions in one-dimensional transport tests, assessed for convergence in two-dimensional advection-diffusion simulations, and demonstrated in fully-coupled drop-in-shear flow simulations covering insoluble, soluble, and partially-soluble surfactant scenarios.

papers.title: Accurate wetting dynamics via a conservative Allen-Cahn based lattice Boltzmann approach for multiphase flows
papers.abstract: In this work we propose a local geometric wetting boundary condition for a conservative Allen--Cahn-based lattice Boltzmann framework. The prescribed contact angle is imposed through ghost phase-field values constructed from a locally reconstructed wall normal and a donor-fluid extrapolation. The ghost-node wetting update is local, geometrically consistent, and compatible with thread-safe large-scale implementations, while phase-field mass is controlled through a separate global volume correction. Validation includes static contact-angle tests, short-time droplet spreading, impact on a hydrophobic surface, and gravity-driven motion through a sharp-edged orifice. The simulations recover the imposed equilibrium angles, reproduce contact-angle-dependent spreading exponents between approximately 1/2 and 1/4, and follow the classical W e1/4 maximum-deformation scaling. The model also captures the transition between capture, release, and release with breakup. The proposed approach provides an accurate and scalable framework for wetting-controlled flows in complex geometries.

papers.title: Vortex dynamics and air entrainment in dam break wave impacting on vertical walls: A multiphase lattice Boltzmann study
papers.abstract: Air entrainment often plays a crucial role in determining impact loads exerted by free-surface wave flows interacting with structures, yet its modelling is often oversimplified in numerical approaches. In this study a two-phase numerical model, based on the Lattice Boltzmann Method coupled to a conservative Allen--Cahn interface-capturing equation is employed to perform direct numerical simulations of dam-break waves propagating over a dry bed and impacting on vertical walls. Access to high-resolution simulations enables a detailed assessment of how accurately resolving both air--water and solid--water interfaces affects local and overall dynamics, as well as quantities of extreme engineering interest. Indeed, the magnitudes and locations of the pressure peaks are strongly affected by wave front deflection and local aeration induced by a small corner vortex. Additionally, comparisons between no-slip and free-slip implementations suggest that the large air cavity formation, commonly observed as trapped inside the reflected jet falling back onto the incoming flow, may be the result of modeling assumptions rather than intrinsic flow physics, again highlighting the key role of near-wall shear in jet breakup dynamics.

papers.title: Poroelastic aquifer response drives seasonal vertical land motion in southern Louisiana
papers.abstract: Coastal Louisiana is sinking, amplifying flooding and land loss, yet the seasonal component of this motion remains difficult to attribute. Satellite geodetic records from Baton Rouge spanning 2004-2024 reveal long-term subsidence of -2.69 +/- 0.69 mm/yr, with a superimposed annual oscillation of 10-15 mm that is in phase with river stage and confined-aquifer hydraulic head. This positive correlation is diagnostic of poroelastic deformation rather than surface loading. A poroelastic model of a semi-confined aquifer driven by hydraulic-head variations reproduces both the long-term and seasonal signals. The seasonal amplitude decreases logarithmically with distance from the intersection of the Baton Rouge Fault and the Mississippi River, as expected for radial pressure diffusion from a flux source. Fault-river intersections therefore act as seasonal conduits into deep aquifers, representing an underappreciated control on coastal land motion that is likely to strengthen as hydrological extremes intensify.

papers.title: Observation of biased random-flux-induced topological phase transition in gyromagnetic photonic crystals
papers.abstract: The interplay between disorder and topological states has attracted growing interest. While previous studies have primarily addressed the effects of geometric or potential randomness, the exploration of topological phase transitions driven by random-flux remains experimentally elusive. Here, we report the first experimental realization of topological phase transitions driven by biased random-flux in gyromagnetic photonic crystals. By stochastically orienting the magnetization of constituent gyromagnetic rods, we implement a disordered Haldane model in which the sign of the next-nearest-neighbor hopping phases is randomly distributed. We demonstrate that the bulk band gap closes when the densities of positive and negative flux are balanced, i.e, restoring time-reversal symmetry in a statistical sense, and reopens when a net positive or negative flux is introduced.
